newsitem.title: UK: Polls show UK's Conservatives gaining ground.
newsitem.headline: Polls show UK's Conservatives gaining ground.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives have slightly narrowed the opposition Labour party's commanding lead with 22 days left until the May 1 election, according to the latest opinion polls published on Wednesday.

An ICM poll in The Guardian newspaper showed the Conservatives up two points to 34 percent while the Labour party was unchanged at 46 percent since last week. The Liberal Democrats were down two at 15 percent.
"The Labour lead over the Tories is 12 points...the lowest since August 1996," the newspaper said. ICM has consistently shown a narrower Labour lead than other polls.
"The figures are adjusted to take account of the suspected unwillingness of some voters to acknowledge their support for the Conservatives," it added.
A Gallup poll in The Daily Telegraph also showed Labour slipping. Its support dropped two points to 51 percent while backing for the Conservatives was down one to 32 percent.
"Labour's lead over the Tories now stands at 19 percent," it said, adding that the swing towards Labour since the 1992 election now stands at 13.3 percent.
Gallup interviewed 1,122 electors by telephone on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday for the survey, while ICM used a random sampling of 1,022 adults, also by telephone on the same days, for their poll.
The Guardian said barely one in 10 voters believes that John Major will head a fifth consecutive majority Conservative government.
